page: Vultr voc-m-32c-256gb-3200s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server configured with 32 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical AMD EPYC cores. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, the processor features hyper-threading, a 32 MB L3 cache, and support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16. The hardware profile includes 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is provided via a bundled 3200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong processing and memory capabilities. The server achieves top-tier performance in stress-ng single-core tests and large-block memory bandwidth, with read speeds reaching 444.47 GB/sec and write speeds at 197.86 GB/sec. Multi-core execution is also robust, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 100562.57 and a PassMark CPU score of 63813.51, both placing in the top 25%. Cryptographic and vector instruction performance is supported by dedicated hardware flags, yielding a PassMark CPU encryption score of 41842.08. Database operations and web serving throughput align with mid-range expectations, while Redis SET operations reach 71.28 million operations per second.

With its high memory density and dedicated CPU allocation, this server offers a balanced resource profile for memory-intensive workloads without the premium of specialized bare-metal hardware. The inclusion of a 3200 GB NVMe SSD provides high-capacity local storage, making it highly suitable for database hosting, large-scale caching layers, and memory-bound data processing. Additionally, the presence of AVX-512 instructions and strong multi-threaded decompression performance supports workloads such as medium-scale LLM text generation, where it achieves 33.69 tokens per second on 7B models, as well as general-purpose enterprise applications.
